label: nyiso 11 cc-steam rebaseline
definition: BASELINE re-established on current main, same keeper config as nyiso 10 (priced interchange + U9 import-node zone remap, gas_monthly_actuals, commitment), after two main fixes landed: (a) load-shed now prices at each ISO's own VOLL (NYISO $2,000, not ERCOT $5,000), (b) the CC steam-turbine outage-coupling fix (9988a79) regenerated campd-unit-outages-NYISO.csv so a combined-cycle CT derates its steam-augmented block when it trips. Effect on the CC-heavy NY stack: CC backs down ~1.7 TWh in 2023 (CC_REGULAR 29.2->28.5, CC_CHP 13.6->12.7), backfilled by imports (16.4->17.9 TWh), gas total 65.1->63.5. Fuel-mix bands HOLD: 2023 vs EIA-923 gas -0.5%, nuclear -0.1%, hydro -0.1% (at 28.40 TWh budget), wind exact; 2025 on the EIA-930 operational basis (EIA-923 2025 is the incomplete prelim M-file) gas -6.4%, nuclear -0.1%, hydro at budget. Price MAE (demand-wtd monthly LMP vs actual RT) 8.20/4.74/5.98 for 2023/24/25 -- essentially unchanged vs nyiso 10 recomputed on the same metric (7.90/4.52/6.23; +0.30/+0.22/-0.25), and the residual SHAPE is identical: 2023 over-prices winter/shoulder (Jan +45, Feb +12, Mar +13), 2025 under-prices the summer/winter downstate tail (Jan -11, Feb -14, Jun -10, Jul -10). Firm-load shed 0 zone-hours all years; zonal pmax 342/198/270. The outage fix is measured ground truth and was NOT tuned around. DIAGNOSIS of the remaining residual (post-solve, no params changed): it is gated by IMPORT-NODE DISCIPLINE, not the outage derate and not CC mispricing. NYC thermal availability is flat across years (5,891 vs 5,782 MW avg, 2023 even higher) and dispatch never exceeds availability (0 capacity-pinned / 0 negative-headroom hours), so the derate did not reduce NYC capacity. The driver is the priced import node: 2023 UNDER-imports (-17.9 vs measured -23.5 TWh, capped ~3.3 GW vs actual 4.9), so NYC backfills with peakers (gas_ct 2,741 vs 1,401 GWh) and -- with the ~1,000 MW NYC interface (HTP+Linden) binding in 200/200 tight summer hours where the import-node price ($33) sits $30 below NYC ($63) -- the energy LP ALREADY prices that downstate congestion; 2025 OVER-imports (-21.9 vs -19.1, diurnal corr -0.86) so NYC under-separates. The locational RCPF overlay (NYISO_RCPF_LOCATIONAL) is structurally correct NYISO market design (tariff-sourced RS4/FERC ER21-502, nested NYCA/East/SENY/NYC reserve demand curves) and stays as-is, but it is GATED ON the energy LP's headroom, which is contaminated by this import-node dispatch error -- so it over-fires in 2023 (NYC $64/yr, Jul $206; would double-count the congestion already in LBMP) and under-fires in 2025. The structural next step is import-node discipline (per-year neighbor-price ladder re-anchor + finer import duration tranches), with the interchange duration band and gas volume as guardrails -- NOT RCPF tuning, which is correct and merely waiting on the upstream physics.
